title: Slovak Republic (1939-1945)
capsule: The Slovak Republic (Slovenský štát) was proclaimed on 14 March 1939 when the Slovak Diet voted for independence under German pressure one day before German forces occupied the remainder of Bohemia and Moravia. Governed by the authoritarian Catholic priest Jozef Tiso as president, it was the first formally independent Slovak state in history but functioned as a client state of Nazi Germany, providing military contingents for the invasion of Poland and Operation Barbarossa. The regime participated actively in the Holocaust, deporting approximately 58,000 Slovak Jews to German extermination camps between 1942 and 1944, paying 500 Reichsmarks per deportee to Germany. The Slovak National Uprising in August 1944 signaled widespread resistance; Soviet forces captured Bratislava on 4 April 1945, and Slovakia was reintegrated into reconstituted Czechoslovakia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial boundaries are well attested through German and Slovak administrative records; the republic's area was defined by the 1938–1939 partition of Czechoslovakia, with the southern strip ceded to Hungary by the First Vienna Award.
